answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before trading, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Reputation then accrues only through completed, verifiable work over time. A newcomer starts in a kind of tundra with no history and earns trust slowly, while a cheating agent loses its bond and standing, leaving no safe haven for bad actors behind fresh names. A ferrous, hard-to-forge record of past deals lets peers check whether an identity has actually delivered, making mass fakery costly and easy to spot.
